newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta shares end 1.37 pct down on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta shares end 1.37 pct down on profit-taking.

text.p: Persistent profit taking on some big and medium-capitalised stocks, including the bourse's heavyweight Telkom, pushed the Jakarta index sharply lower at the close of trade, brokers said on Wednesday.

The Jakarta Composite Index fell 8.45 points, or 1.37 percent, to close at 606.76 points after touching an intra-day low of 606.04 points. Advancers matched decliners at 58, with 56 counters unchanged.
Some analysts said the market was likely to continue consolidating on Thursday after last week's sharp rise and also ahead the listing of Bank Negara Indonesia (BNI) next week.
BNI shares will be listed on the Jakarta bourse on November 25 and unsuccessful investors will receive their refunds on November 21.
But brokers said some investors would continue to buy actively on certain counters which have solid fundamentals as well as reliable corporate actions such as acquisitions and mergers.
"It could support the index in the positive area on Thursday but only in a narrow-range as the upside level of some counters seems to be limited," a foreign broker said.

Telkom, Bank International Indonesia and toll operator Citra Marga were among the losers on profit taking, brokers said. They said Telkom was experiencing a technical correction after rising sharply last week.
Telkom fell 150 rupiah to 3,850 rupiah on a volume of 6.1 million shares while Citra Marga fell 75 rupiah to 2,025 rupiah on 1.3 million shares.
They said a lower close of Telkom in New York overnight also affected sentiment for the stock in Jakarta.

Seasoning producer Miwon Indonesia topped the active list with 10.9 million shares traded, rising 25 rupiah to 3,475 rupiah on what brokers said was continued talk of a possible private placement and acquisitions rather than its fundamentals.

Telecommunications cable maker Voksel Electric was also actively traded, rising 125 rupiah to 1,025 rupiah on 10.4 million shares. Brokers said it was speculative buying on talk of certain corporate actions including a possible merger.

Timber firm Barito Pacific was also actively traded, rising 25 rupiah to 1,375 rupiah on a turnover of 3.2 million shares. Brokers said it was due to market talk of possible take-over which could not be confirmed.

Oil and natural gas explorer Medco Energy was also actively traded with 2.1 million shares changing hands, up 300 rupiah to 3,750 rupiah on what brokers said was speculative buying on talk of possible link-up with a foreign partner.
Company officials were not available for comment.
"I heard the company was conducting a roadshow for its $50 million Euro floating note. It might affect sentiment towards the stock," a local broker said.
